headline_marked: Hackers claim [[19 million Pathao users' data leaked]] and demand $400,000
headline: Hackers claim 19 million Pathao users' data leaked and demand $400,000
summary: A cyber group claims to have stolen 133GB of sensitive user information, including NIDs and addresses, demanding a ransom to prevent its release.
details: A hacking group claims to have stolen the personal data of approximately 19 million Pathao users. The leaked information allegedly includes mobile numbers, emails, National ID (NID) numbers, driving licenses, locations, Facebook identities, and home addresses.

The attackers are demanding $400,000 from Pathao to prevent the release of the data. According to the cyber security platform Daily Dark Web, the claim was first brought to light on X (formerly Twitter) with screenshots of the data on the Dark Web.

Pathao confirmed in a statement that some personal information, including names, email addresses, and phone numbers, was accessed by attackers. The company stated that the incident was detected and brought under control immediately after it was discovered.

To secure their systems, Pathao temporarily took critical systems offline on October 4, which caused temporary service disruptions. They have since engaged external cyber security experts to protect their systems and are working to stabilize the platform.

The hackers claim to possess 133GB of data containing 250 million records across 591 databases. This includes over 19 million NID numbers, driving license details, and approximately 5.7 million home addresses.

Beyond user data, the group claims to have accessed internal business information, including employee records, administrative access documents, bank account details of merchants, and transaction records.

Cyber security expert Tanveer Hassan Zoha urged Pathao to conduct an independent digital forensic investigation and preserve all digital evidence, including servers and access logs, to ensure the same doesn't happen again.

headline_marked: DP World to [[operate Chittagong Port's NCT for 15 years]] amid protests
headline: DP World to operate Chittagong Port's NCT for 15 years amid protests
summary: The Dubai-based firm will invest over ৳1,000 crore in modernization, while the port authority will receive an advance fee of approximately ৳600 crore.
details: The Chittagong Port Authority has signed a 15-year agreement with Dubai-based DP World to operate the New Mooring Container Terminal (NCT), the largest terminal in the port.
The deal, signed at the Invest Bangladesh office in Dhaka, was executed as a government-to-government (G2G) agreement on a public-private partnership (PPP) basis.

DP World is expected to invest over ৳1,000 crore in modernization, equipment, and technology over the first 10 years. The port authority will receive a one-time advance fee of approximately ৳600 crore.
The NCT handles 44% of the port's total container traffic. It is approximately one kilometer long and can accommodate four large seagoing container ships and one small vessel simultaneously.
The agreement was met with protests from left-wing organizations like CPB and BASAD in Dhaka, where police used batons to disperse the crowd. Protests also erupted in Chittagong.
Port workers and labor unions have opposed the lease to a foreign operator, calling the NCT a profitable terminal. The government has assured that workers will not be harmed by the DP World takeover.
Under the terms, DP World must fulfill several conditions, including forming a local company and providing environmental clearances, before taking over the terminal within the next six months.
The Chittagong Port will receive a revenue share of 40% to 67% based on different revenue levels from container operations.
caption:
DP World takes over Chittagong Port's largest terminal in a 15-year deal, but the signing was marred by police action against protesters.

The Chittagong Port Authority has signed a 15-year agreement with Dubai-based DP World to operate the New Mooring Container Terminal (NCT), the largest terminal in the port.

The deal, signed at the Invest Bangladesh office in Dhaka, was executed as a government-to-government (G2G) agreement on a public-private partnership (PPP) basis.

DP World is expected to invest over ৳1,000 crore in modernization, equipment, and technology over the first 10 years. The port authority will receive a one-time advance fee of approximately ৳600 crore.

The NCT handles 44% of the port's total container traffic. It is approximately one kilometer long and can accommodate four large seagoing container ships and one small vessel simultaneously.

The agreement was met with protests from left-wing organizations like CPB and BASAD in Dhaka, where police used batons to disperse the crowd. Protests also erupted in Chittagong.

Port workers and labor unions have opposed the lease to a foreign operator, calling the NCT a profitable terminal. The government has assured that workers will not be harmed by the DP World takeover.

Under the terms, DP World must fulfill several conditions, including forming a local company and providing environmental clearances, before taking over the terminal within the next six months.

The Chittagong Port will receive a revenue share of 40% to 67% based on different revenue levels from container operations.
